description: Temperate smallholding country: coopers, reeves and road-traders, and a market every place is a day from.

appearance.weaver: Sat at the loom, and not stopping it for you.
appearance.cooper: Hands pale with shavings, a half-hooped barrel between the knees.
appearance.carpenter: A pencil behind one ear and sawdust in the crease of both sleeves.
appearance.widow: Neat, grey, and entirely composed. Black worn past the point of mourning.
appearance.child: Small, unbothered, and entirely unsurprised to see you.
appearance.labourer: Big hands, borrowed boots, asleep in the chair until you came in.
appearance.brewer: Sleeves rolled past the elbow, forearms scalded pink.
appearance.netmaker: Knotting by feel, watching you instead of the work.
appearance.cook: Flour to the wrist, and a knife they have not put down.
appearance.server: Carrying four things and looking for somewhere to put two of them.
appearance.drover: Smells of the road and of somebody else's cattle.
appearance.traveller: Boots by the fire, coat still on, ready to be somewhere else.
appearance.harpist: Tuning something that will not stay tuned in this weather.
appearance.shopkeeper: Counting the shelf again, having lost the count once already.
appearance.porter: Waiting to be told which of two crates goes first.
appearance.herbalist: Sorting cuttings into piles that look identical to you.
appearance.apprentice: Young, watchful, and plainly not supposed to be talking to you.
appearance.striker: Shoulders like a door, deaf on the side nearest the anvil.
appearance.priest: Unhurried in the way of somebody whose day has no appointments in it.
appearance.acolyte: Trimming lamps, and glad of the interruption.
appearance.mourner: Sat where the light is worst, and not looking up.
appearance.soldier: Off duty, boots off, belt hung on the bedpost.
appearance.sergeant: Awake, dressed, and unimpressed by the door opening.
appearance.recruit: Standing straighter than anyone else in the room.
appearance.miller: White to the eyebrows, shouting a little out of habit.
appearance.carter: One boot up on a sack, resting a leg that has been walked on all day.
appearance.groom: Talking to a horse in the voice most people save for children.
appearance.farrier: Apron scorched through in three places, hands black to the wrist.
appearance.tallyman: A slate, a stub of chalk, and a very poor opinion of your timing.
appearance.farmhand: Up to the shins in straw, and glad of a reason to stand still.
appearance.watchman: Awake at the wrong end of the day, and making sure you know it.
appearance.signaller: One eye on the window the whole time.
appearance.caretaker: Sweeping something that does not need it, slowly.

lore.title: The Long Weather
lore.premise: The old roads still run between the holdfasts, though fewer people walk them each year. Something in the weather has turned, and the villages have begun keeping their own counsel.
lore.era: the late years of a long decline

ambient: The wind moves across the country.
Somewhere behind you, a bird you cannot name calls twice and stops.
The road here is older than anything built beside it.

mill: Coarse-ground, and still warm from the stones.
Unmilled, with the chaff still in it.
Swept up from under the runner stone.
barn: Unmilled, with the chaff still in it.
warehouse: Undyed linen, wound on a wooden core.
Heavy, and worth more than it looks.
A twist of paper holding two dozen.
smithy: A sack of it, light as nothing.
Offcuts and failures, kept for remelting.
inn: Cloudy, and stoppered with a rag.
shop: Undyed linen, wound on a wooden core.
Forty feet of it, waxed against the wet.
apothecary: Bundled and labelled in a small hand.
temple: Better than tallow, and kept for feast days.
barracks: A twist of paper holding two dozen.
ruin: Old currency, of a mint nobody here uses.
farmhouse: Unmilled, with the chaff still in it.
In a sealed crock, and still good.

shop: Forty feet of it, waxed against the wet.
A bundle of six. They smell of the rendering shed.
Dented, but the shutter still works.
Heavy wool, patched at one shoulder.
A twist of paper holding two dozen.
Struck often enough to have worn a groove.
smithy: Well balanced, meant for wood rather than war.
Second-hand. Somebody's initials are on the pommel.
Rust has been scoured off it more than once.
apothecary: Smells terrible. Closes a cut in a day.
Cloudy, and warm to the touch.
A paper packet, tied with thread.
Three drops. No more, the label insists.
inn: Straw mattress, shared room, no questions.
stable: Enough for a week on the road.
Faded to no colour at all.

crops: Cut green and tied with its own straw.
Grows thick at the foot of the stalks, where the shade sits.
forestFloor: Deep green, and damp all the way through.
Pale, and growing in a rough ring.
Dry twigs, gathered by the handful.
marsh: Sodden, and it holds far more water than it looks able to.
Bitter to the nose, and said to keep flies off.
tallGrass: Whatever was worth taking from a hand's width of meadow.
Shaken loose into a twist of cloth.
reeds: A bundle of them, still wet at the ends.
The brown heads, which burn slowly and smell of nothing.
bush: Dark, and they stain everything they touch.
flowers: Picked with enough stem to be worth putting in water.
deadTree: Split from a trunk that has been dead long enough to be dry.
stump: Prised off a stump with a thumbnail.
Amber beads, tacky in the warmth.
rock: It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
snow: It will not last, and it knows it.
